chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Abdullah ibn Bahr, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A slave girl absconded from her masters, so she went to a tribe other than her own tribe, and she claimed that she was a free woman. So a man married her. Then her master captured her afterwards, and she had given birth to children. He (peace be upon him) said: If the husband establishes the proof that he married her on the basis that she was a free woman, her children will be freed, and the people will take their slave girl. If he does not establish the proof, his back will be struck (for judicial beating), and his children will be enslaved.
ai.seo_question: What is the status of children born to an escaped slave girl who married a free man?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the juristic resolution for a slave woman who escapes and marries a free man while claiming freedom, highlighting the critical role of the husband's good faith. If the husband proves he married her believing her to be free, the children are emancipated and the master retains the woman; otherwise, the man is flogged and the children revert to slavery. This ruling underscores the Shia legal principle of balancing the rights of the master with the status of offspring based on the certainty of the marriage contract's validity.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Abdullah Bin Bahr, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A slave girl absconded from her master, so she went over to a tribe other than her own tribe, and she claimed that she was a free woman. So a man leapt upon her and married her. So her master appeared after that and she had given birth to children’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the husband can establish the proof that he had married her upon a stipulation that she was a free woman, her children would be free, and the people would go with their slave girl. So if he were not to establish the proof, his back would be pained, and his children would be enslaved’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from ‘Abd Allah ibn Bahr from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about the case of a slave girl who runs away from her masters, comes to another tribe and claims that she is free. A man in a hurry comes forward, marries her and her master then succeeds to find her out when she has already given birth to children. He (the Imam) said, ‘If he can establish testimony that he has married her as a free woman her children are free, otherwise, he has caused himself a back pain and his children become slaves.’”
